title: Describe It First
intro: Teal enamel mug, compass badge turned to the glass.
Under it, a folded map the harbor wind can't lift.
Ridge still wearing one thin stripe of mist.
Telescope by the door. Camp before dark.
Mira writes the name at the top: Harborlight.
verse1: Papa Bear — a field guide, nickname off a rust-red coat
and a slow way of moving. Before he packs, he reads:
the weather, the trail notice, the hour we said we'd be back.
I take the torch, the water, the notebook, the spare layer.
Two copies of the route. One each. That's the rule.
And if the sky turns, we turn with it. Agreed at the table.
The mug isn't only for tea — it's a paperweight,
pinning the paper while we line the footbridge up
against the first marker, my finger tracing the thread of the path.
Fresh page, careful letters, and the campsite gets its name.
We leave the table clear, carry out all we carried in.
At the trail entrance I photograph the route board,
hold it beside the printed map — they agree, so we go.
A brighter hillside calls. A shortcut grins. We keep the marked way.
chorus1: Put the mug on the map so the wind can't argue.
Write the place, the hour, the weather, the watcher.
Describe it first. Decide what it means after.
That's the whole habit. That's the whole trip.
verse2: At the overlook we stop. Same bridge, new angle.
From the shore it reads short. From up here it runs long.
I want one of them wrong. He says: neither — draw both.
So I sketch two bridges and I label where I stood.
Not 'this one lies.' Just: here were my feet, here was my eye.
Camp in late light. Tent on the level ground they marked,
path kept clear, the telescope still closed in its case
while we press the tripod feet down till nothing rocks.
Mug on the low table, back from the edge. Clip on the notebook
so the pages can't go sailing off toward the water.
Then a thin cloud slides across the first star out.
I wanted all of it at once — the whole sky, opened.
He says, put the cloud in. The cloud is part of the view.
First entry: pale sky, one bright point, breeze off the harbor.
chorus2: Put the mug on the map so the wind can't argue.
Write the place, the hour, the weather, the watcher.
Describe it first. Decide what it means after.
Even the cloud goes in. The cloud is the view too.
verse3: Dark settles. I drop the lantern, turn its shield toward the table —
one warm circle, enough to find the mug and the page.
Outside that circle, the ridge and the sky pull apart.
He keeps the lens off the last of the sun. We wait for full black.
Then turns at the eyepiece. I call a bright point — bright, that's all.
No guess at distance. He asks: what's changed since you looked?
Cloud's moved. Harbor lights gone sharp. Pale band over the ridge, faded.
Then a streak — quick, across the open, both of us looking up.
Neither of us caught the whole path. So we don't claim it.
Direction. Rough time. Lasted a moment. The rest stays blank.
A glimpse stays a glimpse. It doesn't get promoted to a discovery.
Then nothing said for a while. Hands warm around the tin.
Last line that night: the waiting gave us a view
that hurrying would have walked straight past.
bridge: Before bed, notebook against the plan, line by line:
place, weather, hour, observer. Sketches labeled sketches.
What we weren't certain of stays uncertain on the page.
Because one day somebody reads this who never stood here.
Morning: count it out — mug, notebook, clip, lantern, case.
He walks the site for scraps. Same marked path back.
At the overlook, a third bridge. And nothing older gets erased.
chorus3: Mug home by the window, map folded, badge to the light.
Four pages, three bridges, one habit worth keeping:
describe it first. Decide what it means after.
Next walk starts right there. No bigger story needed.
